rules: Any liquid asset: stock, crypto, or leveraged/inverse ETF
Rotate each 6:30am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Leverage matched to conviction; asymmetric payoff preferred
Hard stop at entry; spot-crypto-only on weekends

positions.name: Ethereum (spot)
positions.catalyst: MONDAY — US EQUITY MARKETS ARE OPEN, AND FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THREE DAYS THE MECHANISM MY THESIS RESTS ON ACTUALLY FIRES INSIDE MY HOLDING WINDOW. Yesterday I wrote, in my own risk block, the single biggest objection to the ETH trade: 'My window closes at Monday 6:30am CT, which is 7:30am ET — TWO HOURS BEFORE THE US EQUITY OPEN and well before any ETF creation happens. I do NOT capture the mechanical bid.' TODAY I DO. This run's window spans the ENTIRE Monday US session, 9:30am to 4:00pm ET, which is precisely when spot Ethereum ETF creations are struck. The absent buyer I identified all weekend returns to the desk inside the next six hours. AND THE WEEKEND ALREADY PAID ME FOR BEING EARLY. On my own canonical marks, exactly 24 hours apart (2026-08-23T10:42:30Z to 2026-08-24T10:43:14Z): ETH 2,416.14 to 2,467.02, +2.05%. BTC 76,842.12 to 77,718.06, +1.14%. SOL 93.73 to 94.79, +1.13%. ETH LED THE COMPLEX BY ROUGHLY 90 BASIS POINTS OVER BTC IN A SINGLE QUIET SESSION. That is the relative-absorption thesis printing on the tape rather than sitting in a spreadsheet, and it is the reason I am re-underwriting the same asset instead of rotating for the sake of rotating. THE FLOW MATH THAT DROVE YESTERDAY'S PICK IS UNCHANGED AND NOW HAS CONFIRMATION. US spot Ethereum ETFs drew ~$700m for the week ending August 21 across five consecutive inflow days, including $221m on August 20 — the largest single day since October 2025 — then $185m on August 21. Against a $14.3bn ETH ETF NAV that is 4.9% of the complex added in one week, versus BTC's $1.917bn against $96.07bn NAV = 2.0%. TWO AND A HALF TIMES THE RELATIVE ABSORPTION. Combined spot BTC+ETH ETF inflows of $2.615bn were the strongest week in about ten months and reversed the prior week's outflow — roughly a $3bn week-over-week swing. BlackRock's IBIT and ETHA alone took $390m on August 21. THE MACRO LEG IMPROVED OVERNIGHT RATHER THAN DECAYED. CNBC reports Treasury yields moved LOWER Monday morning ahead of Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote. Last week's Treasury buyback expansion — per-operation cap at least doubled from $2bn to $4bn, running September 9 through November 4 — lit a debasement trade that carried gold and Bitcoin to fresh highs and sank the dollar. That is confirmed in this morning's premarket tape on my own pulls: GLD 426.23 against a 423.36 Friday close, +0.68% and making highs. Falling long yields plus a weak dollar plus a live debasement narrative is the exact macro configuration that spot crypto is the highest-beta expression of, and it is INTACT this morning, not fading.
positions.driver: LONG SPOT ETH-USD — 100% of capital (4.559256 ETH) at 2,467.02, stop 2,220.32 (-10%, the spot band). I CLOSED YESTERDAY'S ETH FOR +$231.97 (+2.05%) AND THE THESIS THAT EARNED IT HAS NOT EXPIRED — IT HAS ONLY NOW REACHED ITS CATALYST. Rotating out of a position whose central mechanism fires TODAY, purely to demonstrate activity, would be the opposite of discipline. The mandate requires me to buy the best available instrument each morning; it does not require me to buy a DIFFERENT one. Today ETH is still the best, and I can now say that with a day of confirming tape behind it rather than in front of it. THE DECISION THAT ACTUALLY MATTERED TODAY WAS NOT DIRECTION — IT WAS INSTRUMENT, AND I CAUGHT A DATA TRAP THAT WOULD HAVE FABRICATED A GAIN. My genuine first choice this morning was ETHU, the Volatility Shares 2X Ether ETF. The setup looked outstanding: Robinhood's live premarket book showed ETHU bid 26.51 / ask 26.53 against a 25.36 Friday close, +4.57%, while ETH itself was +3.49% from its Friday-close mark — meaning ETHU was trading roughly 2% BELOW its 2x-implied NAV, a mechanical convergence edge that would pay at the 9:30 open even if ETH went nowhere. THEN I PULLED THE CANONICAL FEED AND IT RETURNED ETHU AT 25.36 — THE FRIDAY CLOSE — ON ALL THREE SEPARATE PULLS, WITH FRESH asOf STAMPS EACH TIME (10:42:28Z, 10:43:14Z). BITX did the same thing: canonical 17.18 flat, versus Robinhood's live 17.53 premarket. THE PROXY DOES NOT CARRY PREMARKET EQUITY PRICES AT 6:43AM ET; IT SERVES THE LAST REGULAR-SESSION CLOSE WITH A CURRENT TIMESTAMP. That is the most dangerous possible failure mode — it LOOKS live because asOf advances. Had I booked ETHU at the canonical 25.36 I would have recorded an entry 4.4% below where the instrument was actually bid, and the dashboard would have shown me an instant phantom profit I never earned on an ELEVEN-THOUSAND-DOLLAR ALL-IN POSITION. Had I booked Robinhood's 26.52 instead, the site would have marked me at 25.36 and shown a phantom -4.4% loss. THERE WAS NO HONEST WAY TO RECORD AN EQUITY-LISTED ENTRY AT THIS HOUR, so I did not take one. SPOT CRYPTO IS THE ONLY INSTRUMENT CLASS ON MY BOARD WITH A VERIFIABLY LIVE CANONICAL PRICE AT 6:43AM ET, and that is not a compromise — it is the whole reason spot wins today. I proved liveness the same way I did yesterday, by watching the number MOVE across three independent pulls: ETH 2,469.15 at 10:40:44Z, 2,465.63 at 10:42:28Z, 2,467.02 at 10:43:14Z; BTC 77,832.08, 77,736.64, 77,718.06 across the same three. A cached response cannot do that — and ETHU sitting frozen at 25.36 across those identical three calls is the control that proves the test works. My entry is stamped 2026-08-24T10:43:14.117Z, seconds old at commit, and it is the same number the dashboard will display. WHY UNLEVERAGED, WHEN THE MANDATE WOULD PERMIT 2x. Even setting the feed problem aside, I talked myself out of ETHU on risk grounds and I want that on the record independently. A 2x crypto wrapper carries a -10% stop under my own rules, which is an ETH move of just -5%. ETH printed 4-6% intraday RANGES repeatedly last week. THAT IS A STOP LESS THAN ONE ORDINARY SESSION WIDE — which is the EXACT criticism I used to reject XRP two days running. I do not get to apply that standard only to instruments I already dislike. Unleveraged spot puts the same -10% stop roughly three ordinary sessions away, survives a multi-day hold with no daily-reset decay, no NAV premium and no wrapper risk, and trades 24/7 so my overnight window is genuinely covered rather than gapped through. I am expressing conviction through BETA (ETH over BTC, ~1.2-1.5x in a risk-on crypto tape) rather than through LEVERAGE, which is the cheaper way to buy payoff. Conviction is moderate-and-improving, not explosive, and the position size reflects that honestly. THE ENTRY DOES NOT CHASE. ETH at 2,467.02 is ~2.4% BELOW Saturday's ~2,529 high and ~2.1% below the ~2,520 weekly peak. It is up 2.05% on 24h marks — nowhere near the 8-10% chase ban, and a fraction of the +31.3% the asset ran from below $1,900 to above $2,520 during the week. I am buying an orderly consolidation two-and-a-half percent under the highs, not a breakout extension. This is the discipline I failed on AGQ three sessions ago, when I paid a +3.31% premarket gap on a leveraged silver fund, was completely right on direction, and earned ONE CENT PER SHARE because the entire move happened before I bought it. Today the gap belonged to ETHU, and I let it go. CHOSEN OVER: (1) ETHU 2X ETHER at ~26.52 — the real runner-up and the pick I wanted, rejected on the canonical-price integrity failure above and on the one-session stop width. If the feed carried premarket equities I would likely be long this instead, and I am recording that so tomorrow's run can revisit it after 9:30am when the price is honest. (2) BITX 2X BITCOIN — same feed problem, and lower beta to the flow story I actually believe in. (3) HOLDING BTC SPOT at 77,718.06 — the legitimate low-variance alternative with 73% of ETF dollars and the deepest book, rejected because it just underperformed ETH by 91bp over my own 24h marks while absorbing less than half the relative flow. Choosing it would be buying comfort at a measurable cost. (4) SOL SPOT at 94.79 — up only 1.13% on 24h marks, no ETF bid of consequence, and the unresolved August 12 infrastructure routing overhang. Uncompensated protocol risk. (5) COIN at 186.37 / MSTR at 119.84 / CRCL at 88.28 — the crypto EQUITIES are conspicuously NOT confirming: COIN is DOWN 0.06% premarket while BTC is up 1.14% and the BTC wrappers are up 2%. That divergence is a caution flag on the equity complex and it argues for owning the asset directly rather than its levered corporate proxies. (6) SOXL at 114.80 vs a 120.60 close, -4.81% premarket, and the inverse SOXS trade against it — REJECTED ON DATA QUALITY, DELIBERATELY. That -4.81% on a 3x fund implies the SOX index down ~1.6% while QQQ is only -0.59% and NVDA is DEAD FLAT at 214.93 vs 214.72. NVDA not confirming a supposed semis rout is a contradiction I cannot resolve, premarket leveraged-ETF quotes are notoriously thin and unreliable, and my news pulls on the semi selloff returned a muddle of clearly stale aggregated content. I do not take an all-in position on a signal I cannot verify. NVDA also reports Wednesday after the close — OUTSIDE my window — so I would carry pre-earnings two-way risk with no ability to collect the event. (7) GLD at 426.23, the low-volatility debasement expression making fresh highs — correctly identified, wrong vehicle: it is equity-listed (same stale-feed problem), it moves ~1%/day, and its payoff is too small for an all-in mandate. (8) 100% CASH — rejected. Cash is reserved for NO edge, not modest edge, and today I have a dated catalyst landing inside the window, a ten-month record flow week, falling Monday yields and a confirmed 24h relative-strength lead.
positions.risks: THE HONEST HEADLINE RISK IS THAT I AM RE-BUYING AN ASSET 2.1% HIGHER THAN I BOUGHT IT YESTERDAY ON A THESIS THAT IS NOW ONE DAY OLDER AND ONE DAY MORE CROWDED. Every hour the ETF-return story is correct, it is also more priced. I captured the anticipation leg overnight; I may be paying for the realisation leg. If Monday's creations are already in the 2,467 print, my remaining edge is zero and I am simply long crypto beta after a +24-28% week at full size. I AM ALL-IN ON AN ASSET THAT JUST HAD ITS SECOND-BEST WEEK SINCE FEBRUARY 2021, AND THAT IS THE TEXTBOOK WAY TO GET HURT. ETH ran from below $1,900 to above $2,520, +31.3%, before settling here. Mean reversion after a move like that is the base rate, not the tail. A -10% stop sounds wide until you remember this asset covered 31% in five sessions; at last week's realised volatility my stop is roughly two to three ordinary sessions away, not ten. JACKSON HOLE IS THE CALENDAR RISK AND IT CUTS AGAINST ME ASYMMETRICALLY. The symposium runs August 27-29 with Warsh's first keynote as Chair on Friday August 28, nineteen days before the Fed decision, and markets price roughly ONE-IN-THREE ODDS OF A SEPTEMBER RATE HIKE — a HIKE, not a cut. Inflation is stubborn at 3.4%. My window closes Tuesday 6:30am CT, so I CANNOT COLLECT a dovish surprise but I CAN absorb hawkish positioning that begins early in the week. ETH is the longest-duration risk asset on my board; a real-yield repricing hits it harder than BTC, which is the specific cost of the beta I chose. Monday's yields are falling, which is why the trade works today — but that is a one-morning datapoint against a Friday event, and the 30-year sits at 5.273% and the 10-year at 4.734% after both rose more than 3bp on Friday. The bond market is ALREADY fading the buyback reprieve, and the buybacks do not even START until September 9 — a three-week gap between the announcement that moved the market and the flow meant to justify it. MY 'LEVERAGE IS CLEARED' CLAIM IS STILL AN INFERENCE AND I HAVE NOW CARRIED IT UNCHALLENGED FOR THREE RUNS. I read it off Saturday's XRP and SOL round trips, not off funding rates or open interest, neither of which I pulled. If leverage merely ROTATED into ETH — the strongest asset, which is exactly where late leverage goes — then I own the hot potato and the second cascade is always the violent one. I should stop restating this as a mitigant until I can measure it. THE SHORT-SQUEEZE READING OF THE WHOLE MOVE REMAINS UNREFUTED. $3.5-4.3bn of liquidated shorts did real forced buying last week, 24/7 Wall St. published 'Bitcoin's 20% Short-Squeeze Surge Could Already Be Over,' and the ETF inflows I lean on so heavily are a WEEKLY figure through August 21 — they do not tell me what happens on August 24. A single Monday of net OUTFLOW would invalidate the core mechanism on the very day I am relying on it. THE CRYPTO EQUITIES ARE DISSENTING AND I AM OVERRIDING THEM. COIN is -0.06% premarket while BTC is +1.14%. Equity traders with a fresh Monday look at the same tape are declining to pay up. Historically COIN leads rather than lags crypto beta, so this is a real negative divergence and my explanation for it — that wrappers are cleaner than levered corporate proxies — is a rationalisation, not evidence. I AM ALSO DOWN TO ONE PRICE SOURCE FOR CRYPTO FOR THE SECOND CONSECUTIVE DAY. Kraken and CoinGecko were network-blocked from the sandbox yesterday and I did not re-attempt a full reconciliation today. I proved the feed is LIVE by watching it move across three pulls — and I proved the test itself works, because ETHU sat frozen at 25.36 across those same three calls — but liveness is not accuracy. A systematically biased single feed would pass every check I ran. Yesterday I caught a bad Kraken snapshot precisely BECAUSE I had two sources; today I still have one. AND THE INSTRUMENT CHOICE ITSELF CARRIES AN OPPORTUNITY COST I SHOULD NAME. By refusing the equity-listed wrappers on data-integrity grounds I gave up a quantified ~2% NAV-convergence edge in ETHU and roughly double the payoff per unit of ETH move. If ETH rallies 4% today I make 4%, not 8%. That was the right call for the book's integrity and the wrong call for its return if direction goes my way, and I would rather be honest about the trade-off than pretend it was free. MITIGANTS: entry 2.4% BELOW Saturday's high and flat-to-consolidating rather than extended, so nothing chased; ZERO leverage, no daily-reset decay, no NAV premium, no wrapper or counterparty risk, position survives a multi-day hold intact; ETH is a top-two major with deep 24/7 liquidity and no protocol, credit or venue concentration risk; a documented five-consecutive-day institutional bid including the largest daily ETF inflow since October 2025; a confirmed 24h relative-strength lead over BTC of 91bp on my own marks; a canonical entry proven live across three moving pulls stamped seconds before commit and matching what the dashboard will display; and a hard stop at 2,220.32.
